description: sieve-native/src/lib.rs check_no_test_keyword() looks for 'environment' appearing as a test name in the parsed form tree. However, it would not catch a script that passes 'environment' as a string argument to another test's match type, or that uses the word 'environment' inside a string literal. More importantly: the compile-time check fires only for the 'environment' keyword — there is no similar enforcement for other undeclared extensions. This is belt-and-suspenders and the runtime guard is also present, but the pattern is inconsistent: if a future extension is added to KNOWN without a corresponding check_no_test_keyword call, it silently becomes available without require.
title: sieve: environment extension compile check only covers test keyword, not match-type/comparator argument
